text:
Jamal: Alert from infra-bot — multiple control-plane heartbeats missing for eu-west3 (started ~2m ago). Prometheus group firing: eu-west3_controlplane_down, api_5xx_rate +120%.
infra-bot: [ALERT] eu-west3 control-plane silence detected. Instance group: rg-euw3-controlplane. Alert id: AB12-9.
Jamal: I'm seeing API 504s from customers in eu-west3, and probes show all control-plane endpoints unresponsive.
Priya: Oncall is paged. @pagerduty — can you confirm incident creation and escalation?
pagerduty: Incident #INC-7842 created and assigned to infra-oncall. Priority: P1.
Emily: Running quick checks — kubectl to control plane is timing out from our runbook bastion.
Alex: ran: `curl -sfS https://controlplane.eu-west3.redwood-infra/v1/health || true` -> no response, connection timed out.
Sasha: Checked cloud provider status: https://status.cloud.example.com — no ongoing degraded services listed for eu-west3 region yet. Opening cloud ticket now.
Priya: Can we confirm if it's a network blackhole between our VPC and cloud provider control plane? Any recent routing changes?
Jamal: No infra changes in last 6h. No recent deploys that touch control-plane paths.
Emily: `ssh` to worker nodes in eu-west3? I can reach a few worker hosts, but kubelet says "apiserver unreachable".
Alex: `kubectl get nodes --context=euw3 --no-headers` shows nodes Healthy at node level but control-plane endpoints not reachable. So control-plane likely down, workers up.
Sasha: That suggests API layer impacted, not the whole region network. Could be control-plane autoscaling failing or a control-plane instance crash loop.
Priya: Immediate plan: (1) open provider-incident, (2) prepare traffic shift to fallback region, (3) validate Dedicated pool capacity in fallback. Who takes which?
Jamal: I'll open provider case and attach diagnostics.
Sasha: I'll check control-plane autoscaler logs and last events cluster-side.
Emily: I'll start capacity check for eu-west1 and eu-central1 for both Hosted and Dedicated pools. If both low, we need to throttle non-critical workloads.
Alex: Heads-up — Dedicated GPU pools in eu-west1 are at ~85% commit; we can absorb ~30% burst but not full load. eu-central1 has more headroom but higher network latency for EU customers.
Priya: For immediate mitigation, recommend shifting 30% traffic to eu-west1 and 70% to eu-central1? That splits risk but will increase cross-region latency. Thoughts?
Jamal: Agree. We should also enable model-fallback to smaller quantized variants to reduce GPU memory and allow more concurrency. Emily can coordinate.
Emily: I'll push temporary runbook: reduce default max_workers for the largest models in eu-central1 and eu-west1, enable quantized variant rollouts. Executing now: `infractl config set models/neox.max_workers=8 --scope=region:eu-central1`
Emily: Also creating throttling rule for non-critical batch jobs: `infractl throttle --tag=batch --region=eu-central1 --qps=50`
Sasha: From control-plane logs: last entries show kube-apiserver OOMKilled on master-1 ~3m ago, then master-2 lost heartbeat ~2m later. Looks like a cascading OOM across controller nodes.
Alex: Can we spin an emergency control-plane instance pool? Provider terraform shows quota available for 2 more masters in eu-west3 but API calls to provision are failing (timeouts).
Jamal: Since provisioning is failing, we need to do traffic-shift without restoring eu-west3 for now. Priya — trigger partial traffic shift?
Priya: Initiating canary shift 50% to eu-central1 and 50% to eu-west1 for control-plane requests. Running: `infractl traffic shift --from eu-west3 --to [eu-central1,eu-west1] --weights [0.5,0.5] --dry-run=false`
infra-bot: Traffic shift job started: SHIFT-2026-07. Estimated propagation: 60s. Rolling by route: api.redwood.ai/eu-west3.*
Emily: Monitor model latency — I'm seeing 200ms tail latency spike for some quantized models in eu-central1 as traffic increases. Scaling workers now.
Alex: Warning — scaling more GPU workers will raise immediate cost and may hit dedicated pool commit. We should set a cost cap and rollback if forecasted spend exceeds threshold.
Priya: Set temporary spend alert: `billingctl set-threshold --team=infra --region=eu-central1 --daily=USD:5000`
Jamal: Noted. Also tagging the incident with "control-plane-euw3" and linking runbook.
Sasha: Provider response: ticket #PRV-552 opened. They see platform network flap affecting control-plane HA group. They've escalated to networking team. ETA unknown.
Priya: Keep customer-facing comms ready. Emily/DOCS can start a brief status note for Customers EU indicating degraded service in eu-west3 and failover to nearby regions.
Emily: Drafting: "We detected a control-plane failure affecting eu-west3. Traffic is being routed to eu-central1 and eu-west1; some users may see increased latency. We're working with provider to restore eu-west3." Will post to status when accepted.
infra-bot: Provider ticket update: PRV-552 — "networking team investigating BGP announcement flaps".
Alex: Immediate action item list: Sasha — continue control-plane log forensics; Emily — capacity and model throttling; Jamal — coordinate provider & comms; Priya — traffic shift oversight & cost caps.
Sasha: On it. Found controller-manager logs referencing kube-scheduler stuck waiting on leader election with timeouts.
Jamal: Good catch. Prioritize leader-election diagnostics; if leader lock is corrupted we might be able to force a new leader after caution.
Priya: I'll hold off on leader eviction until provider confirms no split-brain risk.
Emily: Status update in 10m with telemetry.
Priya: Confirming current incident state: FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS. Customers routed out of eu-west3.
pagerduty: Incident #INC-7842 updated: FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS -> MONITORING.
Jamal: Thanks team. Keep this thread for all updates and post major milestones to #incidents-summary.
Sasha: Provider just acknowledged packet loss on peering fabric — working on remediation.
Emily: Monitoring shows error rates falling to ~20% over the shifted regions. Latency stable-ish.
Priya: Closing initial triage — next check in 15m for recovery or further action.
Jamal: Created follow-up task: ACTION-1432 — post-mortem and capacity plan for eu-west3.
infra-bot: Incident notes and logs archived to case storage: /incidents/1967454321/; provider ticket PRV-552 linked.
